children: Average daily ethanol production in the U.S. rose from the prior week, although it landed at the low end of forecasts from analysts surveyed by Dow Jones this week.

In its weekly report published Thursday, the Energy Information Administration said that average daily ethanol production for the week ended Oct. 9 was 1.065 million barrels a day. That's up 12,000 barrels a day from the previous week.
Analysts surveyed by Dow Jones this week had forecast average ethanol production between 1.065 million barrels a day and 1.095 million barrels a day.

Stockpiles were reported as rising for the week, with the EIA pegging inventories at 23.94 million barrels. That's up 199,000 barrels from the prior week. Analysts surveyed by Dow Jones had mostly forecast stocks to fall this week, with estimates landing between 23.49 million barrels and 23.89 million barrels.

CBOT corn futures were flat in midday trading, at $4.94 a bushel. RIN prices have been declining since the EPA announced its new proposal to reallocate 100% of the volume of renewable fuels not blended due to small refinery exemptions--which is seen as supportive to both U.S. farmers and renewable fuel producers.
